applies_to: EVAPCO eco-Air air-cooled and adiabatic fluid coolers and condensers with AC (NEMA-style) fan motors on VFDs.
summary: Same eco-Air PLC as the EC edition but for units with conventional AC fan motors, so the per-EC-fan objects are unused. BACnet IP runs on the Ethernet port and BACnet MS/TP on the RS-485 terminal shared with Modbus RTU. The object list covers enable and state, temperatures, setpoints, fan-speed limits, adiabatic pre-cooling stages and remote fan-speed control.
notes: BV 13-76 and AV 31 and AV 49-100 are EC-fan objects and do not apply to AC-motor units, so they are left out.
The 2022 US edition (COMM22NEMA) lists the same core objects; this file follows the newer 2025 EU edition.

source.title: EVAPCO Controller User's Manual Addendum - Communications Guide AC Motor Edition

integration.summary: Select BACnet MS/TP or Modbus RTU for the serial port on the HMI (BACnet IP is always on the Ethernet port), set addresses under Service > BMS & Network, then use BV 0 to enable the unit from the BMS. Read AV 16, AV 0 and the common alarm and write AV 3 for the process setpoint; remote fan speed works through BV 77, AV 101 and AV 105.

minimum_points.name: bnEnableUnit
minimum_points.why: BMS enable/disable when configured for BMS enable

minimum_points.name: bnUnitState
minimum_points.why: Operating state and reason it is off

integration.enable: Write BV 0 bnEnableUnit = 1 (only works when the unit is configured to be enabled via BMS); AV 16 = 4 means off via BMS.
integration.remote_sensors: Remote fan speed: BV 77 bnRemoteEnable = 1, AV 101 bnRemoteSource = 2 (Communication), then write AV 105. AV 103/AV 104 set the fallback speeds used if the analog speed input is lost.
setup: Default communication parameters are on page 1 of the panel wiring diagram.
Switch the unit off, log in at Service level, open Service > BMS & Network, change values and hold Update for 3 s; the HMI and PLC restart.
The serial port is either MS/TP or Modbus RTU; BACnet IP and Modbus TCP both run on Ethernet.
gotchas: Writable parameters are stored in the PLC's non-volatile memory, rated for about 100,000 writes; never write them cyclically.
Points marked for adiabatic units (pre-cooling valves, flush, wet-stage timers) can be ignored on dry-only units.
